sections.name: Stingwings
sections.card:
Summary: A fast, flying mutant insect with a scorpion-like tail that ends in a deadly sting. You often meet them in swarms, in groups of up to five, and their erratic flying makes them formidable.
Weak points: It is fragile and can be taken down in relatively few shots even at mid-level, but it is extremely fast and hits fairly hard. Its speed and erratic movement make it very hard to hit without V.A.T.S.
Looks like: A large mutated insect with extended mouthparts and a scorpion-like tail ending in a bulbous sting. A glowing stingwing has a body that glows from absorbed radiation.
Tips: Expect a dive-bombing attack: it circles you, rushes in to hit once, then goes back to circling, and sometimes it rushes at you in single file. Their nests are large clusters on the ground and walls that ooze bright yellow sap, and when you approach one several stingwings come out to defend it. At higher levels the stingwing chaser, the toughest kind, is fast, hits hard and attacks together with its group.

sections.name: Mole rats
sections.card:
Summary: A fast, territorial burrowing rodent, found from the Red Rocket truck stop all the way to the Glowing Sea. Compared to many other enemies mole rats are generally weak, but a swarm can hide from your sight and attack from behind.
Weak points: The standard mole rat has a mere 15 hit points and can be killed with a single hit from most weapons. A rabid mole rat is tougher and its bites fester, causing damage over time, but it remains a weak opponent.
Looks like: A bald, pink animal with large front teeth and small eyes, from the size of a house cat up to a large dog.
Tips: Mole rats in the Commonwealth tunnel to avoid you or to close in unseen, but a faint outline of their tunnel can be seen as they move. They retreat into a tunnel if you stand somewhere they cannot reach, such as on top of a car. Some are landminers with fragmentation mines strapped to their backs, and those detonate on impact and hurt anything close.

sections.name: Bloodbugs
sections.card:
Summary: A mutated mosquito that attacks in swarms, stabbing you with a needle-like proboscis and drinking your blood, then spitting the blood back at you for a large amount of radiation damage.
Weak points: Damaging its blood sac makes it lose its spit ability, though the sac is restored if it is given enough time. Its proboscis cannot get through power armor, so against power armor it is left with largely ineffectual stings and its acid spit.
Looks like: About two feet long and muddy brown, with six long limbs, one pair of wings and a long pointed proboscis between two compound eyes. The rare red widow bloodbug has a body tinted red.
Tips: A dead brahmin drained of blood and covered in oversized stings is a sign that bloodbugs are nearby. They cling to trees, walls and ceilings while unaware of you, so a seemingly empty room can hold a whole swarm. Once alerted they spread out and surround you, but if most of the swarm is destroyed before it reaches you the survivors will often retreat.

sections.name: Radscorpions
sections.card:
Summary: A big, fast, aggressive mutated scorpion with a poisoned stinger and the ability to burrow. It can deal a large amount of physical and poison damage in only a few hits, and most are found in the Glowing Sea.
Weak points: Their only weak spot is their relatively small face. Weapons with armor-piercing mods, or the Penetrating legendary modifier, help against their armored exoskeletons.
Looks like: A much bigger version of the emperor scorpion, with powerful claws and a poisoned tail. Albino ones are white, deathskull ones are reddish, and glowing ones glow green.
Tips: Fight them from a distance if you can. If you shoot one from afar it burrows and comes up close to you, often in melee range, but standing on rocks or on metallic or wooden surfaces stops them tunnelling there. Deathskull radscorpions level with you, so they cannot be pacified, and they are among the most dangerous creatures in the Commonwealth.

sections.name: Yao guai
sections.card:
Summary: A ferocious mutated black bear with razor-sharp claws and teeth and a nasty temperament. Wild yao guai attack nearly any other animal or person they meet, deathclaws included.
Weak points: Unlike many other creatures, yao guai do not take increased damage from being shot in the head. The stunted yao guai, with minor malformations, is less of a threat than the other kinds.
Looks like: A large mutated bear. Albino ones are much lighter in colour, rabid ones have red welts on their sides and face, and the dusky yao guai is darker with more pronounced scars.
Tips: Every one of its attacks staggers you, even if you block it, so melee fighting is hard, especially with slow weapons or against a group; time your attacks or you can get stuck in the stagger while it strikes again. They appear as often by day as by night. A dusky yao guai levels with you and is immune to the Animal Friend perk, so it can be an issue at any level.

sections.name: Mirelurks
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated crustaceans of the swamps, coasts and sewers that mostly come in groups and, in most kinds, have a thick shell that is hard to penetrate even with powerful ballistic weapons. They bury themselves in dirt or mud, and from a distance the rounded back of a shell looks like a large smooth rock.
Weak points: The face is unarmored but a small target, and a charging mirelurk often lowers its head to protect it, though the face is exposed once it starts close combat. Its extremities are also more vulnerable than the rest of the body, though not as much as the face.
Looks like: Most adult mirelurks have a shell and pincers like a horseshoe crab, and the hunter looks like a lobster. A glowing mirelurk has a glowing underside and a buildup of radiation in its eyestalks.
Tips: Crippling one set of a mirelurk's legs greatly reduces its mobility, and crippling both sets leaves it unable to move or attack, even face to face with you. Mirelurks have no way to protect themselves against mines or any attack from below. Their thick shells make melee hard because they hide their weak points as you strike, so melee weapons with the legendary modifiers penetrating or exterminator's are useful.

sections.name: Raiders
sections.card:
Summary: Hostile gangs found all over the Commonwealth, most thickly around Boston, organised by seniority and ability within the gang. They viciously defend their turf from anything not in their gang.
Weak points: A common raider is the weakest of the cannon fodder, armed with pipe guns and little health, and survives only a few hits even from basic weapons. Raider veterans are among the toughest, with a high health pool and higher tier weapons, and they are almost never encountered alone.
Looks like: Raider scum wear crudely made welded armor and leather armor, wasters and veterans can wear combat armor, and some scavvers wear raider power armor.
Tips: Psychos are melee-dependent, chem-using raiders that charge you and may throw grenades. Survivalists hide behind objects and blindfire around them, and take well aimed shots when they change position. Like other human enemies, raiders will not chase you into Boston Common: they say the area is deadly and retreat.

sections.name: Sentry bots
sections.card:
Summary: The heaviest class of combat robot, and one of the rarest and most difficult robots to defeat: fast, agile, heavily armed and tough enough to take a direct hit from a mini nuke. The usual loadout is a missile launcher and a minigun.
Weak points: After engaging you for too long it enters a cooldown, blasting steam out of its back and exposing its dual fusion cores, and hitting the exposed fusion cores is the best way to damage it. With the Penetrator perk you can target and destroy the cores in V.A.T.S. without waiting. Unlike other robots it has no combat inhibitor.
Looks like: A bulky robot about as tall as a human in power armor and nearly twice as wide, whose torso can rotate independently of its legs. Gunner sentry bots have a faded green tint.
Tips: If it loses both main weapons it starts its self-destruct sequence and charges you, and it also explodes on death with the force of a mini nuke, so keep your distance. It often charges into close combat if you come too near, which makes melee weapons a poor choice. It drops at least two fusion cores when destroyed.

sections.name: Assaultrons
sections.card:
Summary: A highly aggressive, fast robot that usually charges you to fight in melee, and most models also carry a laser in the head unit. The basic Assaultron is typically found close to old military bases and roadside transports.
Weak points: The head is almost always behind a retractable layer of armor plating, so headshots do reduced damage, but the plates peel back while the laser charges, which is your chance to hit the head directly. Crippling the head permanently takes away its laser, and destroying its legs removes its speed advantage, though it keeps coming by crawling.
Looks like: A robot with claws for hands and a head unit that gradually becomes surrounded by red electric energy as the laser charges. The dominator variant has a darker finish and twin blade arms.
Tips: The laser takes around 6-7 seconds to charge, then the robot stops in place and fires a constant blast for 2-3 seconds that can seriously injure even a high-level character caught off guard and not behind cover, so get behind cover. A badly damaged but working Assaultron can detonate in an explosion as damaging as a mini nuke, and killing it first gives a normal death. The dominator variant uses a stealth field that stops V.A.T.S. targeting until it is in melee range, and only crippling its torso stops that for good.

sections.name: Mister Gutsy
sections.card:
Summary: A combat robot, the combat version of the civilian Mister Handy, whose weapon varies from a 10mm submachine gun to a laser weapon or sometimes a flamer. Its 10mm submachine gun is able to shred low-level characters, and even ones in power armor, in seconds.
Weak points: It has several targetable sections: the torso, right eye, middle eye, left eye, combat inhibitor, thruster and arms. If an eye is broken its firing accuracy suffers, and disabling the thruster slows it down and removes its strafing ability. Breaking all of the arms makes it attempt a suicide rush on you.
Looks like: A robot with a torso, three eyes, arms and a thruster, and the words "Mister Handy" written on the back of its body.
Tips: The Killshot perk makes the right and middle eyes easier to hit in V.A.T.S., but not the left eye. A neutral Mister Gutsy turns hostile if you look at it while wearing power armor with a targeting HUD mod installed. The Lieutenant and Major Gutsy carry lasers and have bigger health pools, and the Colonel Gutsy appears once you reach level 46 or higher and levels with you.
